coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: 1470 Owens Street
record.summary: 1470 Owens Street is a parking structure at Mission Bay, designed by Watry Design to serve multiple UCSF life-science buildings and the adjacent Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices. DataSF Assessor records and Watry Design's own project page both date its completion to 2020.

changes.text: 23 routine building permits (alterations, revisions, deferred submittals, fire or utility work and similar) now appear under Building permits in this record's research notes instead of on its timeline. 10 permit cost figures now show as the valuation of the matching permit entries under Building permits, not under Costs. Earlier change-log entries about these permits stay in the log until it is archived at launch.

The earlier row (2026-09-24) "The cable-barrier installation permit's cost was revised to $65,000." says the permit's cost was revised. DataSF DBI Building Permits, permit 201904178265: "estimated_cost":"65000.0","revised_cost":"65000.0". The two fields are equal, so the figure is the permit's declared valuation, not a revised or actual construction cost. The earlier row is left as written.

The earlier row (2026-09-24) says a permit for "two temporary trailers" was completed (2022-08-09). DataSF, permit 202205023408: "description":"temporary(2) construction of trailers on the roof of adjacement parking garage at 1470 owens st.","status":"complete","completed_date":"2022-08-09". The "(2)" could be a count or another code; the number of trailers is not stated. The earlier row is left as written.

The earlier row (2026-09-24) "The parking garage's permit carried a $6,000,000 valuation, unchanged from filing" says the designer's page gives $22,400,000 but its source column lists only the permit. Watry Design, 1470 Owens Parking Structure: "Project Status: Completed 2020 Parking Stalls: 317 Levels: 4 ... Total Project Cost: $22,400,000". This is a designer-reported total, not a DBI figure. The earlier row is left as written.

A WRNS Studio page titled "UCSF Parking Structure" lists a 2012 completion, 10 stories and 627 stalls for what it calls the Owens Street Parking Structure, with no street number. Watry Design lists 1470 Owens as completed in 2020 with 4 levels and 317 stalls, so the WRNS page is treated as a different building; which building it depicts is not confirmed.

The record now says the garage was designed by Watry Design and serves UCSF life-science buildings and Kaiser's medical offices. Before, it called it a UCSF parking structure designed by WRNS Studio, but Watry's own page names Watry as designer and lists the owner only as 'Developer'. The map use changed from institutional to commercial (the Assessor's class). The unsourced Kaiser address was dropped, the Assessor citation now points at the record for this parcel, the ERRCS administrative permit no longer carries a 'planned' status, permit descriptions no longer place every added security item on levels 2-4 (DBI places only the blue phones there), the $6,000,000 permit figure is described as the permit's unrevised valuation, and the aerial photo's caption and credit no longer say 'from a departing flight', which the Commons page does not state (the photographer's name is now cited to his Commons user page).

changes.text: The permit to install a ground non-electric double-faced sign carried a cost of $5,000.

Over-the-counter alterations, deferred submittals and revisions tied to the garage's construction (cable barriers, curtain walls, fire service, pile testing and more) had each set the garage's status. Status is now set only by the garage's own new-construction and completion events. One outlying permit moves to a separate list of building permits.
A permit for cable barriers at the parking garage was recorded complete.
A permit was issued to install cable barriers at the parking garage.
The cable-barrier installation permit's cost was revised to $65,000.
A permit was issued for curtain wall installation at the parking garage.
The curtain wall installation permit was marked complete.
A permit for two temporary trailers on the garage roof was completed.
The rooftop trailers permit's cost was revised to $75,000.
A permit for fire water service and sprinklers at the garage was completed.
A permit was issued for fire water service and underground sprinklers at the garage.
The fire water and sprinkler permit's cost was revised to $10,369.
A permit for metal stairs at the garage was recorded complete.
The metal-stairs permit's cost was revised to $130,000.
A deferred permit for the parking garage's metal stud wall framing was issued.
A permit for a green screen at the garage was recorded complete.
A permit was issued to demolish the existing surface and grade for the new parking lot.
The site-demolition and grading permit's cost was revised to $100,000.
A permit for evacuation signage at the garage was recorded complete.
A permit was issued for miscellaneous metal rails at the garage.
The metal-rails permit was recorded complete.
A permit for the garage's aluminum fin facade reached complete status.
A permit was issued for the garage's aluminum fin facade.
A permit was issued for an auger cast pile load test ahead of the parking garage's construction.
The pile load test permit was recorded complete.
The pile load test permit's cost was revised to $50,000 from an initial $25,000 estimate.
A permit for the garage's security screen system reached complete status.
A permit revision was issued adding a fire pump room, security screens and landscaping to the garage plan.
The fire pump room and landscaping revision permit was recorded complete.
A permit relocating the garage's backflow preventer and fire department connection was completed.
A parking-signage permit for the garage was completed.
The parking-signage permit's cost was revised to $10,000.
An administrative permit confirmed the garage's parking structure needs no ERRCS system.
A permit adding an ejector pump to move wastewater to the manhole was completed.
The ejector-pump permit's cost was revised to $20,000.
A permit revising the garage's pile caps and grade beam reinforcement was issued.
The garage's structural-reinforcement revision permit reached complete status.
A permit was issued for production auger cast piles at the future parking garage site.
The auger cast piles permit's cost was revised to $2.3 million from an initial $900,000 estimate.
The auger cast piles permit reached complete status.
DBI records the site's future use as a public parking garage, previously vacant.
A deferred plumbing permit for the new garage building reached complete status.
A deferred plumbing permit for the new garage building was issued.
A permit adding security cameras, blue phones, card readers and smoke detectors was completed.
A permit was issued to add security cameras, blue phones, card readers and smoke detectors.
The parking garage's new-construction permit was issued.
The parking garage's main construction permit reached complete status.

The parking garage's permit carried a $6,000,000 valuation, unchanged from filing. That is the permit's own valuation, not a revision and not the project's total cost, which the designer's page gives as $22,400,000.
A permit was issued to add wind screens at the garage's 4th-floor elevators.
The 4th-floor elevator wind-screens permit was recorded complete.
The wind-screens permit's cost was revised to $16,000.
A permit was issued for aluminum composite panels on the parking garage.

1470 Owens Street added as a parcel-backed record: a parking structure (designed by Watry Design, per its own project page) serving nearby UCSF life-science buildings and the adjacent Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices, identified during the same positioning review. Confirmed via the designer's own project page and a parking-facility listing. DataSF's Building Footprints layer has no footprint at all for this parcel, so the Assessor parcel boundary is used directly.

open_questions: Exact month/day of the 2020 completion is not sourced, only the year.

A WRNS Studio project page titled 'UCSF Parking Structure' (wrnsstudio.com/projects/ucsf-parking-structure/) lists a completion of 2012 and describes a 10-story, 627-stall, 223,602 sq ft structure that it calls the 'Owens Street Parking Structure', without giving a street number. Watry Design's page for 1470 Owens lists completion 2020, 4 levels, 317 stalls and 109,200 sq ft, and the Assessor's year built for this parcel is also 2020, so the WRNS page is treated here as describing a different, earlier building, not this parcel. Which building the WRNS page depicts is not confirmed.

As of 2026-09-29, no source found dates the start of physical construction; the timeline carries the permit issue date (2018-10-03) and completion (2020) only. Watry Design's page lists its owner as 'Developer', so no source read names UCSF as the garage's owner.

WRNS Studio was earlier named as the designer; the only cited designer page (Watry Design) names Watry, and the WRNS 'UCSF Parking Structure' page has not been confirmed to be this garage, so WRNS is not stated here.

record.notes: 1470 Owens Street -- a parking structure serving multiple UCSF Mission Bay life-science buildings and the adjacent Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices, designed by Watry Design (its project page lists the owner only as 'Developer'; no source read names the garage's owner); garage entrance on Nelson Rising Street off Owens St (ParkChirp). Features a green-wall security screen and 25 EV charging spaces (per the designer's own project page); ParkChirp lists it as a parking facility. Identified by Pier & Point during a map review of open ground between already-mapped sites. DataSF's Assessor data (dataset wv5m-vpq2) lists blklot 8709019 at 1470 Owens St; this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary (the DataSF Building Footprints layer has no captured footprint at all for this parcel, likely a parking-structure gap in that dataset).
